labels.cancelled_note: The run was cancelled by the user; only the items processed before cancellation are reported.
labels.method_text: Each file was opened read-only and hashed in a single pass with the selected algorithms. PDF files were then parsed without being modified: every saved revision, its dates and producer, digital signatures, fonts and producer fingerprints were recorded, and pages of consecutive revisions were compared visually. Every action was written to a hash-chained audit log.
labels.next_ok: No action needed for this file.
labels.next_attention: Review the findings below with your examiner before relying on this file.
labels.next_problem: Do not rely on this file until the examiner has explained the problem.
labels.summary_ok: The file was hashed and checked. The checks applied found no issues.
labels.summary_attention: The file was hashed and checked. Some points need attention.
labels.summary_problem: The file could not be fully examined or shows a serious problem.
labels.fingerprint_text: This fingerprint identifies the exact content of the file. Any change, even of one character, would produce a different value.
labels.timestamp_pending: Pending — the time-stamping service could not be reached; add it later with the timestamp command
labels.not_signed: This PDF is not digitally signed.
labels.timeline_note: Dates are those stored in the file (Info dictionary, else XMP); the software that saved it can set them freely. Without usable dates the revisions are spaced evenly.
labels.sig_trust_note: The signer certificate, its chain and its revocation status were not validated: a mathematically valid signature does not show who controlled the key.
labels.fp_no_match: No producer or editor from the databases was recognised.
labels.history_once: The document was saved once%{tool}; the file keeps no record of later changes.
labels.history_many: The document was saved %{count} times; the last change was made %{elapsed} after creation%{tool}.
labels.history_many_nodate: The document was saved %{count} times; the dates stored in the file do not show when the last change was made%{tool}.
labels.history_caveat: This information comes from the document itself and is not proof on its own.
labels.pdfs_multi_revision: PDFs with more than one revision
labels.item_reports_skipped: Items without report files (--item-reports flagged, no issues found)

EMPTY_FILE.title: Empty file
EMPTY_FILE.shows: The file contains no data (0 bytes).
EMPTY_FILE.does_not_prove: It does not show whether the file was emptied deliberately or created empty.

EXTENSION_MISMATCH.title: Extension does not match content
EXTENSION_MISMATCH.shows: The name ends in .%{extension} but the content starts with the signature of a %{detected} file.
EXTENSION_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: Renaming is common and often innocent; it does not by itself prove an attempt to hide content.

EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.title: Executable content under another name
EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.shows: The content is a %{detected} program although the name ends in .%{extension}.
EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.does_not_prove: It does not show that the program is malicious; analyse it in an isolated environment.

DUPLICATE.title: Duplicate content
DUPLICATE.does_not_prove: Identical hashes show identical content, not who copied the file or when.

UNREADABLE.title: File could not be read
UNREADABLE.does_not_prove: It does not show that the file is damaged; permissions or locks can cause this.

PARSER_FAILED.title: PDF analysis did not complete
PARSER_FAILED.shows: The isolated analysis of this file stopped before finishing (reason: %{reason}, exit code %{exit_code}). The file was hashed and its integrity record is complete; the PDF structure, revisions and visual comparison were not fully analysed.
PARSER_FAILED.does_not_prove: It does not show that the file is malicious or forged: damaged, unusual or very large files can exhaust the time or memory limits. Re-run with higher limits or examine the file manually.

VISUAL_CHANGE_BETWEEN_REVISIONS.title: Visible change between revisions
VISUAL_CHANGE_BETWEEN_REVISIONS.shows: Rendering revision %{from_rev} and revision %{to_rev} gives different images on page(s) %{pages} (largest changed share %{changed_ratio_max}); pages added: %{pages_added}; pages removed: %{pages_removed}. The changed areas are outlined in the comparison images.
VISUAL_CHANGE_BETWEEN_REVISIONS.does_not_prove: Incremental updates are normal when forms are filled, documents are signed or comments are added. It does not show who made the change, when, or with what intent.

VISUAL_DIFF_SKIPPED.title: Visual comparison not performed
VISUAL_DIFF_SKIPPED.shows: The page-by-page visual comparison of the revisions could not be made: %{reason}.
VISUAL_DIFF_SKIPPED.does_not_prove: It does not show that the revisions look the same or differ; the structural analysis of the revisions is unaffected.

INCREMENTAL_UPDATES.title: Incremental updates
INCREMENTAL_UPDATES.shows: The file contains %{revisions} revisions: the original save plus later updates appended to the end of the file. Each earlier version can be extracted and compared.
INCREMENTAL_UPDATES.does_not_prove: Incremental saving is normal when a PDF is filled in, signed, annotated or re-saved by many programs; it does not show who changed the file or that a change was improper.

METADATA_INFO_XMP_MISMATCH.title: Info dictionary and XMP metadata disagree
METADATA_INFO_XMP_MISMATCH.shows: The %{field} value differs between the Info dictionary (%{info}) and the XMP metadata (%{xmp}).
METADATA_INFO_XMP_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: Some programs update only one of the two metadata stores; a mismatch shows that the file was processed by more than one tool or edited, not that its content was falsified.

MODDATE_BEFORE_CREATIONDATE.title: Modification date earlier than creation date
MODDATE_BEFORE_CREATIONDATE.shows: In revision %{revision}, the %{source} modification date (%{modification}) is earlier than the creation date (%{creation}).
MODDATE_BEFORE_CREATIONDATE.does_not_prove: Wrong computer clocks, time-zone handling bugs and metadata copied from a template can cause this; it does not by itself show deliberate backdating.

REVISION_TIME_GAP.title: Time gap between revisions
REVISION_TIME_GAP.shows: Revision %{to_rev} is dated %{gap} after revision %{from_rev} (according to their modification dates).
REVISION_TIME_GAP.does_not_prove: Metadata dates are written by the editing software from the computer clock and can be set freely; the gap does not prove when the changes were really made or by whom.

PRODUCER_CHANGED_BETWEEN_REVISIONS.title: Different software between revisions
PRODUCER_CHANGED_BETWEEN_REVISIONS.shows: The producer changes from “%{before}” in revision %{from_rev} to “%{after}” in revision %{to_rev}.
PRODUCER_CHANGED_BETWEEN_REVISIONS.does_not_prove: Documents legitimately pass through several programs (for example a signing or form tool); this shows a change of tool, not who used it or why.

EDITOR_FINGERPRINT.title: PDF editor fingerprint
EDITOR_FINGERPRINT.shows: Revision %{revision} carries the fingerprint of a PDF editor: %{label} (metadata %{matched_on}: “%{value}”).
EDITOR_FINGERPRINT.does_not_prove: Editors are also used for legitimate tasks such as filling in, signing, rotating or compressing a document; the fingerprint shows which software saved the file, not what was changed.

ONLINE_EDITOR_OR_UNLOCKER.title: Online editor or protection-removal tool
ONLINE_EDITOR_OR_UNLOCKER.shows: Revision %{revision} was saved by %{label} (metadata %{matched_on}: “%{value}”), a web service or a tool that removes PDF protection.
ONLINE_EDITOR_OR_UNLOCKER.does_not_prove: These services are often used innocently (to merge, compress or convert files); the match shows the file passed through such a tool, not that its content was altered. Metadata can also be typed by hand.

PRODUCER_STRUCTURE_MISMATCH.title: Structure does not match the declared producer
PRODUCER_STRUCTURE_MISMATCH.shows: Revision %{revision} declares %{label}, but its internal structure differs from what that software is known to write: %{traits}.
PRODUCER_STRUCTURE_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: Optimisers, repair tools and later re-saves change the structure without changing the metadata, and versions of the same program differ; this suggests the declared producer is not the last program that wrote the file, not that the content was falsified.

UNKNOWN_PRODUCER.title: Producer not in the fingerprint database
UNKNOWN_PRODUCER.shows: The producer “%{producer}” (revision %{revision}) is not in the fingerprint database used for this analysis.
UNKNOWN_PRODUCER.does_not_prove: The database covers a limited set of programs; an unknown producer is not suspicious in itself.

XREF_OFFSETS_INCONSISTENT.title: Cross-reference data inconsistent
XREF_OFFSETS_INCONSISTENT.shows: In revision(s) %{revisions}, the cross-reference data does not point at the objects it lists, or startxref points to the wrong place. The objects were located by scanning the file, and every case is listed in the warnings.
XREF_OFFSETS_INCONSISTENT.does_not_prove: Buggy writers and damaged transfers also produce wrong offsets; this shows the file was not written cleanly by a standard tool, not that it was manipulated.

HYBRID_XREF.title: Hybrid cross-reference
HYBRID_XREF.shows: Revision(s) %{revisions} use both a classic cross-reference table and a cross-reference stream (/XRefStm), so older and newer readers may see different objects.
HYBRID_XREF.does_not_prove: Some mainstream writers produce hybrid files for compatibility; the analysis compares both views and reports differences in the warnings.

DATA_AFTER_FINAL_EOF.title: Data after the end of the file
DATA_AFTER_FINAL_EOF.shows: %{bytes} bytes follow the last %%EOF marker. PDF readers ignore them, so they are not displayed.
DATA_AFTER_FINAL_EOF.does_not_prove: Transfer tools and some writers append padding or log data; this does not show that the extra bytes are hidden content, but they should be examined separately.

CONTENT_CHANGED_AFTER_SIGNATURE.title: Content changed after signing
CONTENT_CHANGED_AFTER_SIGNATURE.shows: Signature %{field} covers an earlier revision; revision(s) %{revisions}, added afterwards, change page content or document structure, which the signature does not cover.
CONTENT_CHANGED_AFTER_SIGNATURE.does_not_prove: The signature remains mathematically valid for the signed revision; this does not show who made the later changes or whether the signer agreed to them. Compare the signed revision with the final one.

SIGNATURE_INTEGRITY_FAILED.title: Signature integrity check failed
SIGNATURE_INTEGRITY_FAILED.shows: Signature %{field} failed an integrity check (%{reason}). digest_mismatch: the signed bytes no longer match the digest stored in the signature; signature_invalid: the signature value does not verify with the signer's public key; byterange_*: the signed byte range does not cover exactly one revision minus the signature itself.
SIGNATURE_INTEGRITY_FAILED.does_not_prove: This shows the signature does not protect the bytes as they are now; it does not show who altered them, and a damaged transfer can also cause it.

SIGNATURE_PRESENT_TRUST_NOT_VERIFIED.title: Digital signature present (trust not verified)
SIGNATURE_PRESENT_TRUST_NOT_VERIFIED.shows: The file contains signature %{field}, signed by %{signer}. Its byte coverage and cryptographic integrity are reported separately.
SIGNATURE_PRESENT_TRUST_NOT_VERIFIED.does_not_prove: This tool does not validate the certificate chain, revocation or the signer's identity; a signature can be technically intact and still come from an untrusted or self-made certificate.

DOCMDP_VIOLATION.title: Changes not allowed by the certification signature
DOCMDP_VIOLATION.shows: Signature %{field} certifies the document with permission level %{level} (1 = no changes, 2 = form filling and signing, 3 = also annotations), but revision(s) %{revisions} contain changes outside that level.
DOCMDP_VIOLATION.does_not_prove: The classification of changes is heuristic and some PDF viewers apply permissions differently; this shows a conflict with the declared permissions, not intent.

JAVASCRIPT_PRESENT.title: JavaScript present
JAVASCRIPT_PRESENT.does_not_prove: Forms often use JavaScript for calculations and validation; it does not show malicious behaviour. Analyse the scripts in an isolated environment.

LAUNCH_ACTION.title: Launch action
LAUNCH_ACTION.shows: %{count} object(s) contain a /Launch action that asks the viewer to open a file or run a program (%{objects}).
LAUNCH_ACTION.does_not_prove: Most viewers block the action or ask first; it shows that an attempt is defined, not that it ran or what it would do.

EMBEDDED_FILES.title: Embedded files
EMBEDDED_FILES.does_not_prove: Attachments are a normal PDF feature; they are not necessarily visible in the document and should be extracted and examined separately.

INVISIBLE_TEXT.title: Invisible text
INVISIBLE_TEXT.shows: Page %{page} draws %{count} text item(s) that cannot be seen: invisible rendering mode (3 Tr), white fill or fully transparent fill.
INVISIBLE_TEXT.does_not_prove: OCR layers on scanned pages and accessibility text are invisible by design, and white text can sit on a dark background; this does not by itself show an attempt to hide content.

TEXT_OVER_SCANNED_IMAGE.title: Text over a scanned image
TEXT_OVER_SCANNED_IMAGE.shows: Page %{page} is drawn mainly by one image that covers most of the page and also contains text; the text is first present in revision %{text_revision}.
TEXT_OVER_SCANNED_IMAGE.does_not_prove: Scanners and OCR software add a text layer to scanned pages to make them searchable; text added in a later revision deserves a visual comparison, but neither case proves alteration.

FONT_ADDED_IN_LATER_REVISION.title: Font added in a later revision
FONT_ADDED_IN_LATER_REVISION.shows: Font %{font} first appears in revision %{revision} and is used by page content there.
FONT_ADDED_IN_LATER_REVISION.does_not_prove: Editing tools add fonts when a form is filled in, a stamp or comment is added or text is legitimately corrected; this shows that text was written in that revision, not that it falsifies the document.

SCANNED_PAGES_STRUCTURE_ONLY.title: Scanned pages: structural analysis only
SCANNED_PAGES_STRUCTURE_ONLY.shows: %{count} page(s) (%{pages}) consist of a single large image without text.
SCANNED_PAGES_STRUCTURE_ONLY.does_not_prove: Changes inside the pixels of an image (for example retouching before or after scanning) are not detected by this structural analysis.

ENCRYPTED_PARTIAL_ANALYSIS.title: Encrypted document: partial analysis
ENCRYPTED_PARTIAL_ANALYSIS.shows: The document is encrypted (/Encrypt). Its structure, revisions and signature byte ranges were analysed, but encrypted strings and streams (metadata, page content, object streams) were not decrypted.
ENCRYPTED_PARTIAL_ANALYSIS.does_not_prove: Encryption is common and legitimate; findings that depend on decrypted content could not be checked and are missing for that reason only.

NOT_A_PDF.title: Not a PDF file
NOT_A_PDF.shows: No %PDF- header was found in the first 1024 bytes, so the file was not analysed as a PDF.
NOT_A_PDF.does_not_prove: The file may be another format with a .pdf name, or a damaged PDF; examine it with a tool suited to its real type.

limitations.SIGNATURE_TABLE_LIMITED: Type detection uses a limited table of common file signatures; unknown types are reported as unknown, not as suspicious.
limitations.TIMESTAMPS_FROM_FILESYSTEM: Modification times come from the file system of the examined copy and may differ from the original source.
limitations.CLEAN_RESULT_IS_NOT_AUTHENTICITY: A result without findings does not prove that a file is authentic or unaltered before acquisition.
limitations.TIMESTAMP_PROVES_EXISTENCE_ONLY: A trusted timestamp proves the audit log existed in this exact form at the stated time; it does not prove that the examined copy matches the original source.
limitations.NO_FINDING_IS_NOT_AUTHENTICITY: The absence of findings does not prove that a PDF is authentic or unaltered: a document can be forged before it is saved, or re-created so that no trace remains.
limitations.FLATTENED_OR_REGENERATED_PDF_LOSES_HISTO: When a PDF is printed to PDF, flattened, optimised or regenerated, its earlier revisions and most editing traces are lost; only its last state can be examined.
limitations.FINGERPRINT_DB_COVERAGE: Producer fingerprints come from a limited database (vendor documentation and files generated by Rakvor); producer strings can be typed by hand, and unknown or spoofed values cannot be recognised.
limitations.SIGNATURE_TRUST_NOT_VALIDATED: Digital signatures are checked for byte coverage and cryptographic integrity only; certificate chains, revocation and the signer's identity are not validated.
limitations.RENDERING_PAGE_CAP: The visual comparison between revisions renders only a limited number of pages per revision; pages beyond that limit are compared structurally only.
